newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.01 up at 41.30 to the dollar in the kerb market on Wednesday amid a depressed dollar demand and will remain firm at these levels in coming days, dealers said.
"Dollar demand is slack these days because of the strength of the stock market and a liquidity crunch among exporters and speculators," dealer Owais Kalia said.

The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last fixed on July 11, was at 40.5200/40.7226 to the dollar. The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates ended unchanged at 2.20 percent. -- Amir Zia 9221-5685192
